correctness.rationale: In KG(5,2), color classes are intersecting edge sets of K5. For each class, any outside edge meeting all its edges is forced into the other class. A singleton edge forces two disjoint other-color edges; for a two-edge star ab,ac the forced edges ad and bc are disjoint. Empty classes are impossible. Intersecting families of size at least three are triangles or stars. A 3-star forces its missing spoke into the other class; that other class must be the full star at the missing leaf (a triangle would overlap and a 3-star there would have a missing spoke the first class cannot cover). Two full stars overlap. A full star can pair with any triangle or 3-star on its four remaining points. Two edge-disjoint triangles necessarily share exactly one ground point. In each allowed case the intersection transversals are already colored, so all zero vertices see both colors. This gives 30 ordered triangle pairs and four 20-member types at weight seven. Each type is a transitive S5-set, and the five full stars are the maximum independent sets, so their pair intersections force Aut(P)=S5. An independent support-first replay oriented bipartite components in every induced nonzero subgraph and filtered for the zero-neighbor requirements; it reproduced 30 at weight six, 80 at seven, the five precise orbit sizes, and the triangle characterization for all 30 optima.
residual_risks: Colors are named and automorphisms act only on graph vertices; quotienting by color swap changes the census. No extension to other generalized Petersen graphs is established.

evidence: P(5,2) and KG(5,2) are the same graph. Gabrovšek et al. give the minimum for the same rule. The outer-independent rule in 2263ae4eab5a requires independent zero vertices and admits double colors, unlike the frozen rule.
In f63f1a00725c each triple class is a full open neighborhood, equivalently a triangle of K5; the two optimal triple classes are edge-disjoint and their centers are disjoint 2-sets.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: For two triangles meeting at one point, the four remaining edges form K2,2 on the exclusive leaves. The two valid splits into intersecting doubletons are by the endpoints on one exclusive side or the other. Selecting which side determines which triangle is color 1, giving an S5-equivariant bijection from optimal class-domination partitions to the named-color triangle pairs. It is an optimum-only correspondence: every weight-seven type has a 4-star, which cannot be contained in any open neighborhood of the cubic Petersen graph.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct contribution is the full named-color census, in particular all weight-seven functions and their four orbits, together with completeness of the five-orbit classification. The optimum value six is already known. The triangle-pair data at weight six have a substantive equivalent overlap with a distinct same-day Resultary class-domination result, as verified by a bijection; I do not credit those optimum data as exclusive novelty or infer priority by publication date. The class-domination polynomial does not count the feasible weight-seven functions.
residual_risks: The 2018 introducing paper and SOR 2021 pp. 173–178 were not available in inspected lawful full text. The similar 2020 Independent Rainbow Domination Numbers of Generalized Petersen Graphs article was also not retrieved. An earlier exact enumeration not established by the inspected evidence remains possible.

value.rationale: The whole weight enumerator and orbit decomposition are natural invariants of the canonical Petersen graph with named independent colors. The four distinct weight-seven families plus the optimum orbit give exact symmetry-reduced data for comparing two-rainbow variants and for testing proposed generalized-Petersen enumerators. Neither the already known minimum nor the adjacent optimum partition calculation provides those data.
residual_risks: One natural fixed graph and rule only; no sweeping assertion about generalized Petersen graphs or novelty of the minimum in isolation.
